'''Christopher John Doleman''' (October 16, 1961 – January 28, 2020) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). '''Christopher D. Foote''' (born December 2, 1956) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (American football)|center]] for 11 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and the [[United States Football League]] (USFL). He was primarily a [[long snapper]] on punt teams during his NFL career.

He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]], starting at center during their [[1980 Rose Bowl]] championship season. He found his niche in professional football as a [[long snapper]] and [[special teams]] member.

In the NFL Foote spent two years each with the [[Baltimore Colts]] and [[New York Giants]], finishing up with five years playing for the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. He retired from football in 1991.

Born and raised in [[Placentia, California]], Dressel played scholastically at [[El Dorado High School (Placentia, California)|El Dorado High School]].<ref name="PFR1">{{cite web| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DresCh00.htm |title=Chris Dressel Stats |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref> He played [[college football|collegiately]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]],<ref name="NFL">{{cite web| url=https://www.nfl.com/players/chris-dressel/ |title=Chris Dressel Stats |website=NFL.com |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref> where, as a senior, he was honored by the [[Gannett News Service]] as a third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].<ref name="GNS 1982 p1">{{cite news |title=Elway, Walker head Gannett all-star squad |newspaper=Poughkeepsie (NY) Journal |author=Joel Buchsbaum |date=November 25, 1982 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/poughkeepsie-journal-1982-gannett-all-am/147558478/ |page=50 |access-date=May 17, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>

Dressel was selected by the [[Houston Oilers]] in the third-round of the [[1983 NFL draft]],<ref name="PFR2">{{Cite web |title=1983 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1983/draft.htm |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=Pro Football Reference}}</ref> and started 30 of 32 games his first two years. He was with Houston for two more years, again appearing in all 32 games, but with no starts. In 1987 he played in one game for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] as a [[replacement player]] during the [[1987 NFL season#The NFLPA strike|NFLPA strike]]. He was out of the NFL completely in 1988.<ref name="PFA">{{Cite web |url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/playerd/dres00200.html |title=Chris Dressel Stats |website=Pro Football Archives |access-date=June 2, 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230502185917/http://www.profootballarchives.com/playerd/dres00200.html |archive-date=May 2, 2023}}</ref>

In 1989 Dressel resurrected his career, initially with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] for seven games, then with the [[New York Jets]] for the last eight games of the season. During the 1990 and 1991 seasons with the Jets he appeared in 15 games each year, starting a total of 10 of them. He finished his career back with the 49ers for one game in 1992.<ref name="PFA"/>

Dressel recorded 111 pass receptions for 1098 yards and 8 touchdowns during his 9 years in the NFL.<ref name="PFA"/>

After his football career, Dressel pursued a real estate career in San Francisco.{{Citation needed|date = January 2016}}
